items.title: George Wein — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: You've got a big commercial name, you got, like a Jamie Cullum or a Chris Boti or something like that

ctx.x: Is there a … something that does to or for an audience when you have different acts on the show and then at the end, everybody comes out and does something together? What is that about?

It all depends. It all depends on the evening and the group. We don't always do that. We don't do that much at all. Sometimes your highlighter is in the middle of a show and the end just fades out. When people are sitting four or five hours listening to music, you don't … maybe the last group's a throw-away, who knows. Maybe it isn't. You've got a big commercial name, you got, like a Jamie Cullum or a Chris Boti or something like that, and before that you might have the Mingus band. But every show is different…
You've been doing this multiple stage thing for a very long time.
